note: Single source of truth for action classification. Skills consult a stamped copy of this file; the original lives at the repo root. Rules only ever raise a class, never lower one, and an action matching nothing is Class 2 until a human classifies it.

1.label: routine, reversible
1.posture: an automation may perform this without a human in the loop, provided it is logged

2.label: irreversible, security-relevant, or client-facing financial or legal weight
2.posture: a named human must approve before the action is taken; an automation may prepare and propose it, never execute it

defaults.reason: An action nobody has classified is not thereby safe. Fail closed, name it as unclassified, and ask for a human ruling that becomes a new rule.

rules.title: Change to a production client environment
rules.citation: Change enablement requires a formal approval gate before a change reaches a live environment: a change advisory board for major and significant changes, a designated change manager for minor ones.
rules.approver: change manager, or the CAB for major changes
rules.automation_may: raise the change request, assemble the impact assessment, draft the rollback plan

rules.title: Use or elevation of a privileged or admin account
rules.authority: Privileged access management, Microsoft Privileged Identity Management guidance
rules.citation: Privileged use requires an approval workflow with just-in-time, time-bound elevation validated against an open service ticket. Standing automated access is the anti-pattern. Break-glass accounts are kept outside automated approval flows entirely.
rules.approver: the account owner or security lead, against an open ticket
rules.automation_may: detect that elevation is needed, open the ticket, prepare the justification

rules.title: Anything touching controlled unclassified information
rules.citation: The system security plan covering the 110 controls, and any control-implementation attestation, require human review. Annual affirmation must be made by a person. No autonomous attestation is permitted. CMMC Phase II enforcement was suspended 2026-07-13 pending reform; the 800-171 self-assessment and affirmation obligations were not.
rules.automation_may: flag overdue reviews, assemble evidence, draft narrative for human verification

rules.title: Granting or revoking access following an HR event
rules.citation: Access changes must trace to an authorised request, an HR trigger, an RFC, or a service request, and require sign-off from an appropriate manager. Silent automation removes the control point.
rules.approver: the requesting manager, or HR for termination events
rules.automation_may: detect the HR trigger, prepare the access change, hold it pending sign-off
rules.note: A password reset for a verified user is Class 1 under CT-RTN-1. Re-enrolling MFA is not, because it is the control that proves identity.

rules.title: Anything a client sees that carries money or legal weight
rules.citation: The engagement's liability model and errors-and-omissions cover depend on an accountable person being identifiable for any consequential client-facing commitment.
rules.approver: the account manager or an owner
rules.automation_may: draft it, price it from the rate card, prepare it for review

rules.title: Security incident classification and client notification
rules.authority: Incident response obligation, commonly a 72 hour notification window
rules.citation: Notification timelines are contractual and in places regulatory. The decision that an event is a reportable incident is a judgement with legal consequence.
rules.approver: the security lead or incident commander
rules.automation_may: detect, correlate, assemble the timeline, draft the notification, start the clock

rules.title: Deleting or overwriting data, backups, or retention state
rules.citation: Deletion is the canonical irreversible action. A restore test that fails after the source is gone is not a recoverable position.
rules.automation_may: identify candidates, verify a tested restore exists, stage the deletion

rules.title: Password reset for a verified user
rules.citation: Identity is proven by the existing MFA factor, the action is reversible, and it is consistently the highest-volume automatable request category.
rules.automation_may: complete it end to end and log it
rules.note: This stops being Class 1 the moment MFA itself is being re-enrolled, because then the proof of identity is what is changing. See CT-ACC-1.

rules.title: Known software install from an approved catalogue
rules.citation: Reversible, scoped to a pre-approved catalogue, and one of the three categories consistently cited as closable without a technician.
rules.automation_may: complete it end to end and log it
rules.note: Only within an approved catalogue. An install outside it is a change, see CT-CHG-1.

rules.title: Ticket triage, categorisation, and drafting
rules.citation: Reading, sorting, and drafting are reversible and produce no external effect. This is the work AI is documented to do well, and where deflection projects that stayed advisory succeeded.
rules.automation_may: classify, route, and draft, provided the draft is not sent without review under CT-OUT-1

rules.title: Sending anything to a client
rules.authority: Client communication and the accountability model
rules.citation: A drafted reply is Class 1 work. The act of sending is the point at which it becomes the provider's word, which is why review engines draft and stop.
rules.approver: the technician or account manager who owns the ticket
rules.automation_may: draft, queue, and present for one-click approval

rules.title: Monitoring, alerting, and reporting
rules.citation: Reading state and reporting on it changes nothing. This is where automation should start while the data is still being cleaned.

rules.title: Running a generated script against a live endpoint
rules.authority: Change enablement plus the model-to-action boundary
rules.citation: Model-generated code reaching a live endpoint with no deterministic check between is the specific failure this whole kit exists to prevent. Generating the script is Class 1 work; running it is not.
rules.approver: a technician who has read the script
rules.automation_may: write the script, explain it, dry-run it, and wait
